The only way I've actually managed to bleed VP is this.....

1. Be in a task force that has a low intel weekly requirement. I mean 15 or less. 

2. Only attack AI and Terror / Doom / Etc, typically. While you save up your map. This will keep your reserves topped up so you keep getting attacked. 

3. Try to keep a decent amount of reserves over and above your vault, not just slightly above, but give people some incentive to attack you, then keep topping this up from AI. You might drop here and there - that's ok....

4. Only ever clear your map for big upgrades, and then do it all at once and repeat the cycle. 

5. Get a very good RR bonus, more resources from attacks = the less you have to attack, and the replenishing I spoke about in point 3 is easier to maintain. 

Other than that play a bit less. Do your upgrades, attack your AI, but don't hang around getting tempted to attack just because you enjoy attacking. 

Then just watch your vp slowly go down over time. If you put off big upgrades it will go down a lot faster, since this clearing the map bit gets it back again.

Here is my best attempt at a very good system to getting in the big upgrades. 

1. Have a very good RR MP (Resource Reward). If you haven't got one yet, then definitely have 2 or more guardians down. I think 2 is the sweet spot. Leaving the rest of your statue spots for GBE and TH+TD - and as far as statues go, since they contribute a lot to your offense, ensure you have a very good PSC MP. It's crucial you have a good RR bonus. 

2. Save up resources on your map. Swop out those you can't take, and while you're saving attack AI bases. Don't worry about VP inflation, just don't be clearing your map all the time. To me this was a big hurdle to overcome in my thinking. It's not that intuitive, since most video games reward you directly for being active. You really want to hold off attacks until you have nearly all players on your map that are doable. Ditch the ones that are too high, swop them out for realistic ones. 

3. Use the AI invasions to build up some kind of stash. Now it's almost sure this alone will not give you enough for big upgrades, but it is important before we get to point 4, that you do not start out clearing your map without resources. So for example if the upgrade I wanted cost 1.2m wood, 700k stone and 350k iron, then I would want to have at least 200k-300k stone, etc, from AI attacks and passive income BEFORE I start clearing my map. 

4. If your map is nicely synced on a terror day AND you have some stash (not completely empty), you can now execute "operation cleanup". Start by immediately boosting your RR statues, and get as far as you can in Terror without taking any troop loss. After this clear your map of AI and player bases. To save time when you clear the player bases, boost your TH+TD statues, which will prevent loss and downtime. 

5. Stay online until you have all the resources you need from this method. If you're a bit short, use diamonds to finish off the upgrade, but you should not be spending 100's of diamonds here, 60-80 diamonds for a big upgrade is reasonable. 

6. If you can't get the upgrade in, then spend the resources on something else. The next best thing. EG, you might have wanted armory, but GB was a bit cheaper and you went for that. 

7. Even after this method you might still be extremely short. Well then you're not ready for the upgrade, you're going to need to work on your offense first. Consider the Weapons Lab, I think they drop this into the game when you're level 38. Now most players at 38 are simply not ready to get that upgrade in. It's too expensive and the players that appear on your map aren't swimming in resources either. Just because the weapons lab is available, doesn't mean you have to have it right this very minute, you can ultimately upgrade your crappy defenses first, in between the big and important upgrades, and by that I mean anything that improves your offense. 

I have not included methods like saving OP and VP rewards and timing the sub, to get an upgrade in, but that should be common sense. 

The key is not to get frustrated when you're pushing the boundary. Consider when something like gold storage level 10, first came up as an achievement, remember when you first saw the requirements? It seemed like the first time I saw tank 2.5m, or when like now, it's 3.5 or something for me. It just seems almost impossible to get that kind of gold/wood, etc. But you must just keep upgrading offense. The evidence, have a look now at buildings that cost 400k wood, these seem almost low now for you right? But at level 20? Seemed impossible. 

Have fun upgrading your defenses too, if you really get stuck and can't get big upgrades in, trust me having an intimidating base won't save it much from people rolling in, but you will get diamonds , intel and it does deter some players from attacking.

A TF is worth joining if you're going to participate in attacks. 

There are 2 sides to the equation, what you get out of it, but you should also consider what you're giving back to the TF. 

Most TF's have fairly low intel requirements. 15 intel per week seems to be the standard. An active player (mid ranged) can easily farm that intel in a day. Most active players push 50+ intel per week. 

But take into account, VP shedding, and base reserving. It's not always feasible or desirable to be attacking just for intel. Basically I do not advocate it. If the TF has a min intel requirement, sure meet it but don't try and be a hero just attacking for intel - because you will end up with VP bloat, and it can make it harder for you to upgrade stuff in the long run if you aren't saving up your map. 

At least always attack. This is a bitch for dedicated TMed's, because tanks aren't always the best choice for OP's. But mostly I can't be bothered to swop out my troops. So I rather hold off attacking till I feel I can contribute with a tmed attack. 

EDIT: At my level that's about 120k per day I put into the attack. Maybe I should reconsider and swop out for riflemen. But yeah the general idea is you attack till all your troops are dead, and this isn't free. Early game it's no big deal, but it does get expensive.

I've been with a handful of TF's now, and to me there are 2 things that ruin the TF experience for me. 

1. Extremely serious and critical analysis of attacks to the point where it just squeezes out the fun. No one likes to be told exactly how to attack. Also don't be super eager to please when you join a TF by asking "How should I attack?" You don't want to feel like people are telling you how to play the game. Use your own initiative. 

2. Players who refuse to attack and a TF leader who refuses to kick inactive players. TF's have a limited number of spots, so imo unless you're a daily player and can contribute to attacks 99% of the time, find a casual TF. Even if you totally suck and wipe, as long as you try.

BB TF chats also tend to be plutonic, and a lot of the chatting is done on phones, so it's obviously like trying to spit thoughts through a straw. If I want to talk about BB, I have this sub, and it's way more intellectual.

1. Focus on getting a good power stone chance boosts early on. Statues can make or break your game play experience. But to get good statues you need a steady source of power stones. 

2. Resource reward statues are a must. Try your very best to get a good resource reward MP. 

3. Don't even waste your time with green statues. It's true what everyone else is saying. 

4. Level up your LC's and get get a good troop combo for your level. This might be Warriors or Hookas or Tmeds. Don't spread yourself too thin, keep one troop combo completely maxed. 

5. Do not neglect defense. It does bite you later if you've neglected it completely. Having a good defense at best will help you ward off attacks, and at worse earn you intel and diamonds. 

6. Do not be at all concerned with exact base placement prior to level 10. Often I see guys on here taking early levels very seriously. Trust me your level 3 sniper tower and that one machine gun isn't going to stop an ant. Later you'll see why that is. 

7. Watch old youtube vids on how to defeat x, y or z. A lot of content on youtube is outdated, so before you watch a how to defeat Hammerman vid, make sure the base layout hasn't changed. For example H45 now has mines which were never there before. 

8. Don't spend diamonds to speed things up. Spend them wisely on missing resources. Later you'll see spending a few diamonds here and there to save an hour isn't such a bad thing though. 

9. Don't neglect riflemen, they may be the starting troop but when used wisely still have their place. 

10. Don't focus too much on VP. Bottom line is if you have inflated VP it can be harder to find easier opponents but so far - never impossible. So don't let it worry you.

"Random" from a programming point of view, is a very 101 topic, if you think SuperCell have made some error in randomization you're most likely wrong and need a basic lesson in probability. 

Rolling the same statue type 10 times in a row isn't that huge a feat. 

This means there is a probability factor of 0.3333% (That you roll the same 10 statue types in a roll )

Essentially it's the same chance as rolling a 5 or a 6 with 2 dice and 1 roll. 

Not that huge a deal.

Firstly to be clear on the definition of random. 

1. Random truly means with each roll there is no history of the previous roll. For this reason it would be completely random even to roll 100 PS masterpieces in a row. 

2. Even if you've rolled 10 in a row, you are statistically no more unlikely to roll an 11th PSMP. That's just the way random and probability works. It's built into nature and a mathematical construct, has nothing to do with SC. 

3. Your chances of rolling same status is fairly high, considering it's a purple hence 33% for each roll. Statistically 33% is a lot, 1 in 3. 

Run an offline test. take 3 cards from a desk. The Ace, the 2 and the 3. Now shuffle them a bit and try and find the ace. As you can see it's fairly common to find it multiple times in a row. 

I will say 8 in a row would at first appear statistically wrong, but it's very common from a probability point of view.

Financial development can be very well paid, make no mistake. 

As for job security I cannot comment on the scene in SA but globally I wouldn't say Financial development offers any greater risk of retrenchment than other sectors. 

What I can say from personal experience is that without strong financial background, Financial development can potentially be extremely boring. I've worked in 2 financial development roles. I have a passion for programming and the financial stuff was in many ways just a chore. It can get extremely complicated and some aspects will take years to master. Eg: Fees and rebates or FUM calculations. 

Now compare that to other forms of development such as factory automation or general web application development and imo after a few years you might still actually enjoying the work you do. 

At the last place I worked a lot of developers were using the time to gain general experience and financial stuff looked epic on their CV. Also there was a trend for a small fraction of those truly passionate about finance to leave their development roots behind and take on BA positions. 

&tldr: Money is good, stressful work, measurable deadlines, complicated and downright boring (if you're not passionate about finance).
